name: git-include
description: A simple way of managing nested git repositories.

paragraphs: git-include is a modern alternative to submodules and git-subrepo. It inlines an upstream repository together with a small marker file into a subdirectory of your repository. That's the whole model:
--recursive, no submodule update, no git-include installation required. Only the person syncing with upstream needs the tool.

git include push rebuilds upstream history from your commits — each host commit that touched the directory becomes an individual upstream commit with its original message and author (even commits made before a pull), and the marker file never leaks upstream.
features: Two-way sync. git include pull merges new upstream work into your tree;
git-subrepo compatible. The marker file is the same .gitrepo format.
